Medley

/MED-lee/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Medley means a mixture of differing things.

Medley means a mixture of differing things. The school talent show closed with a medley of pop songs from five different decades, stitched together so one hit flowed straight into the next.

Worked Example

For the neighborhood potluck, Uncle Theo brought what he called his garden medley, a roasted mixture of carrots, beets, zucchini, and whatever else had ripened that week. No two forkfuls tasted quite the same, and the pan was scraped clean by sunset.

The dish is a mixture of many differing vegetables tossed together in one pan, which is exactly what a medley is.

How Medley Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

assortment

assortment: a varied collection of things

mixture

mixture: a combination of different things

hodgepodge

hodgepodge: a jumbled mix of many kinds

Antonyms

uniformity

uniformity: complete sameness with no variety

monotony

monotony: dull, unchanging sameness

How Strong Is It? — blend → jumble → medley

blend vs. medley

blend vs. medley: A blend combines its ingredients so smoothly that the separate parts disappear, while a medley keeps each differing piece recognizable inside the mix.

jumble vs. medley

jumble vs. medley: A medley is a pleasing mixture of differing things, but a jumble is a disordered heap with no arrangement at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — medley

Root — medley: from Old French medlee, a mixing, ultimately from Latin miscere, to mix

Put it together

Put it together: Medley came into English from Old French medlee, 'a mixing,' which traces all the way back to Latin miscere, 'to mix.' The word arrived as a single piece rather than a prefix-plus-root construction, but its mixing root lives on in several other English words.

Use the root in a new word: meddle

Use the root in a new word: meddle: Neighbors warned him not to meddle in the twins' argument, using a word that began as 'to mix yourself into' other people's business, the same mixing root behind medley.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, often informal

Medley names a mixture of differing things, as in a medley of songs, flavors, or colors. Do not confuse it with melody, which is a single musical tune; a musical medley actually strings several different tunes together into one performance.
